claims.claim: Physical automation requires machines to perceive and localize in dynamic environments; Ouster's combined lidar, stereo vision, compute and perception software maps directly to that sensing-to-action bottleneck across robotics, industrial and infrastructure use cases.

Multi-modal breadth improves scenario robustness but does not make Ouster a unique bottleneck owner because camera-only, radar, alternative lidar and integrated OEM stacks remain substitutes by use case.

factors.name: bottleneckControl
factors.basis: Perception is necessary for many autonomous systems, but Ouster does not uniquely control the sensing stack.

factors.name: scenarioRobustness
factors.basis: Robotics, industrial automation and smart infrastructure diversify application demand.

factors.name: substitutionResilience
factors.basis: Sensor fusion broadens capability while competing modalities and suppliers constrain exclusivity.

risks.risk: Successor bottleneck shifts from sensor availability to integration cost, perception software quality, compute efficiency and OEM qualification.

causalEdges.mechanism: autonomous systems require reliable environment sensing and localization
causalEdges.falsifier: target applications standardize on lower-cost modalities that materially reduce lidar/stereo demand

causalEdges.mechanism: multi-modal platform can reduce integration burden and cover more environmental conditions
causalEdges.falsifier: customers prefer modular best-of-breed stacks or integration complexity offsets platform benefits

unknowns.unknown: Post-acquisition StereoLabs revenue contribution and cross-sell economics are not isolated in current evidence.

claims.claim: Operating traction is real, but financing dilution is a material present risk: Ouster used its ATM in the first half and sold an additional 3.62 million shares in July for about $191.9 million net proceeds.
The Stereolabs acquisition expands capability but adds integration risk and equity issuance; profitability remains incomplete despite stronger Q2 revenue and gross margin.

factors.name: financingDilution
factors.basis: ATM issuance and the July equity offering increased share count to fund operations/growth.

factors.name: integrationRisk
factors.basis: Stereolabs adds useful vision/software capability but requires integration across products, teams and go-to-market.

factors.name: profitabilityConversion
factors.basis: Q2 gross margin improved while GAAP net loss and adjusted EBITDA loss remained negative.

risks.risk: Repeated equity financing can dilute per-share upside if operating cash generation does not catch up with growth investment.
Sensor-market competition and modality substitution can pressure pricing even as physical-AI adoption grows.

causalEdges.mechanism: external capital bridges cash needs until operations self-fund
causalEdges.falsifier: sustained positive free cash flow eliminates recurring equity issuance

contradictions.claim: Strong product revenue growth and margin improvement coexist with continued losses and equity issuance.
contradictions.resolution: Both are supported; growth quality is improving but has not yet eliminated financing dependence.

unknowns.unknown: Future financing cadence and fully integrated Stereolabs profitability are not established.
